descriptions.WEEE_COLRATE: WEEE collection rate: tonnes collected / 3-year mean tonnes put on market (Eurostat env_waseleeos, EE6)
descriptions.WGI_RL: Rule of Law estimate (World Bank WGI)
descriptions.PV_CAPTURE: PV panels collected / modelled central arisings, capped at 1 (Eurostat EE_LE_PVP vs Layer B)
descriptions.CE_EMP: Employment in circular-economy sectors, % of total (Eurostat cei_cie011)
descriptions.CE_INV: Private investment in circular-economy sectors, % GDP (Eurostat cei_cie012)
descriptions.WEEE_RCYRATE: WEEE recycled and prepared for reuse / WEEE collected (Eurostat env_waseleeos, EE6)
descriptions.WEEE_HH_KGCAP: WEEE collected from households, kg per inhabitant (Eurostat env_waseleeos, EE6)
descriptions.MW_RECYCLING: Recycling rate of municipal waste, % (Eurostat cei_wm011)

rho_notes.a1: Reuse needs preparing-for-reuse standards and re-certification rules (C1), refurbishers and a used-module market (C3), and buyer acceptance of used modules (C4); acceptance becomes decisive for old vintages in H3 (Tsanakas et al. 2020).
rho_notes.a2: Cascading through repowering is enabled by repowering rules and warranty transfer (C1) and by second-use demand (C3, C4).
rho_notes.a3: Export hinges on the used-equipment/waste boundary and shipment rules (C1) and on their enforcement (C2); it needs only traders (C3).
rho_notes.a4: Bulk recycling is already mandated by the WEEE Directive (C1 moderate) and needs treatment capacity (C3).
rho_notes.a5: High-value recycling needs recovery targets or CRM crediting (C1) and, above all, recyclers and secondary-material buyers (C3), a dependence that falls as the technology matures (Heath et al. 2020; Deng et al. 2019).
rho_notes.a6: Formalised take-back needs EPR scheme design (C1), certified collection and leakage control (C2), installer and PRO actors (C3), and willingness of owners to hand over modules (C4).
rho_notes.a7: Disposal is the default where regulation, enforcement and public participation are weak; strong institutions reduce its feasibility (inverse).
